item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a strong public dashboard, sector scorecard, or recurring audit trail showing the presidency using metrics to track and correct social-service performance across health, education, WASH, or social protection. The positive evidence is concentrated in a few administrative and programmatic pockets, not a system-wide feedback loop. The strongest available pattern is still partial technocratic cleanup alongside persistent underfunding, opaque procurement, and weak implementation.","evidence":[{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes","summary":"The PEQIP education project was built around stronger information systems, decentralized planning, and merit-based teacher recruitment, including more qualified female teachers and support for students with disabilities.
